summary.en: Compare brute force, a crossing-interval recursion and Kadane while keeping the answer nonempty.
summary.bn: ব্রুট ফোর্স, দুই ভাগের পদ্ধতি ও Kadane দিয়ে সর্বোচ্চ যোগফলের অবিচ্ছিন্ন অংশ বের করো।

notes: The Maximum Subarray implementations use C17 and the numeric limits stated in their input contracts.

practice.statementHtml: Read n (1..16) and n changes (-99..99), after Enter n and values:. Print best = S, range = L R using half-open indices. Keep the earliest start, then earliest end, on ties.
hints: Enumerate starts before ends and replace only on a strict improvement.

practice.title: Maximum Subarray: justify the decisions
practice.statementHtml: Explain why the recurrence or decision rule for Maximum Subarray covers every valid candidate, and why evaluation terminates.
hints: A subarray contains consecutive input positions.
practice.answerHtml:
Before processing index i, ending is the best sum ending at i-1, and best is the best sum inside [0,i). Any interval ending at i either contains only a[i] or extends an interval ending at i-1. The recurrence chooses the better of those exhaustive possibilities. Updating best then compares the previous prefix answer with the best newly ending interval.

At the beginning, the only nonempty interval in the first-element prefix is that element itself. The invariant therefore holds after initialisation. Each iteration preserves both meanings. When the final index is processed, every possible nonempty interval ends somewhere in the processed prefix, so best covers all candidates. The loop terminates because i increases toward n.

For divide and conquer, the three location cases are exhaustive. A crossing interval must use a suffix of the left half and a prefix of the right half. Their choices are independent, so taking each greatest sum maximises their total. The nonempty base case returns its sole value. Induction over interval length proves the recursive results.

practice.title: Maximum Subarray: derive resource bounds
practice.statementHtml: Derive the time and auxiliary-space bounds for the implementations of Maximum Subarray. Separate input, working storage and returned information.
hints: Best ending and best overall are separate quantities.
practice.answerHtml:
Brute force performs n+(n-1)+...+1 interval extensions, which is Θ(n²). It needs Θ(1) auxiliary storage. The recursive method does two half-size calls plus linear crossing scans. Its recurrence T(n)=2T(n/2)+Θ(n) gives Θ(n log n) time. The active recursion path uses Θ(log n) stack space.

Kadane visits each value once and uses a fixed number of arithmetic operations and comparisons per visit. Its time is Θ(n), and its two totals use Θ(1) auxiliary space. Returning interval boundaries adds only a few indices. Copying every candidate interval would destroy that constant-space advantage, so store boundaries and copy only the final answer when needed.

The loop bounds remain linear for positive, negative and mixed input. There is no sorting or early finish. Arithmetic width remains a separate concern: summing many large changes can overflow an int. The exercise bounds of sixteen values between -99 and 99 keep all intermediate sums safe, including the quadratic reference and crossing scans.

quiz.prompt: What is the required maximum sum of [-8,-3,-6]?
quiz.explanation: A nonempty answer chooses the largest single negative value.

quiz.prompt: What does ending mean in Kadane?
options: Best sum anywhere in the full array
Best nonempty sum ending at the current index
quiz.explanation: The endpoint restriction makes the two-candidate transition possible.

quiz.prompt: When should Kadane restart instead of extending?
options: Whenever the current value is negative
When the previous ending sum is negative
quiz.explanation: Adding a negative previous sum makes the current singleton better.

quiz.prompt: Which recursive case can two child maxima miss?
options: A singleton in the left half
An interval entirely in the right half
quiz.explanation: A crossing optimum combines a left suffix and a right prefix.

quiz.prompt: How many nonempty intervals does quadratic brute force extend?
quiz.explanation: For each start there are n-start possible ends.

quiz.prompt: Which cost belongs to the crossing-scan divide-and-conquer method?
quiz.explanation: Each level has linear scanning work across balanced recursive nodes.

quiz.prompt: Why is sorting before maximum-subarray search invalid?
options: It changes which values are consecutive
quiz.explanation: The answer must refer to a contiguous interval of the original sequence.

quiz.prompt: After the -1 change, what is Kadane ending?
quiz.explanation: Extending gives 2, better than restarting at -1.

quiz.prompt: What nonempty best sum does Kadane return for two negative days?
quiz.explanation: The second singleton improves the best from -8 to -3.

quiz.prompt: What sum remains best after the final -5?
quiz.explanation: The earlier interval 3,-1,4 remains best at 6.

keyPoints.en: A subarray contains consecutive input positions.
Nonempty maximum sums can be negative.
keyPoints.bn: খালি অংশ না নিলে সর্বোচ্চ যোগফল ঋণাত্মকও হয়।
Kadane নতুন শুরু আর আগের অংশ বাড়ানো তুলনা করে।

keyPoints.en: Crossing intervals combine a left suffix and right prefix.
keyPoints.bn: মাঝ পেরোনো অংশে বাঁয়ের suffix ও ডানের prefix লাগে।

keyPoints.en: Best ending and best overall are separate quantities.
keyPoints.bn: এখানে শেষ হওয়া সেরা যোগফল আর মোট সেরা যোগফল আলাদা।

examQuestions.question: Show the worked Maximum Subarray trace, including each rejected candidate or completed dependency. Explain the final answer.
examQuestions.answerHtml:
ivalueendingbest
0-2-2-2
1333
2-123
3466
4-516

The running totals explain why a temporary negative value inside the answer need not end it. The -1 day is worth keeping between profitable days 3 and 4. Kadane discards an earlier prefix only when its total would make every future extension worse. It does not discard every individual negative number.
